learning_outcomes.text: Provide the student with basic knowledge about computer-aided design techniques.
Develop the ability to see or imagine geometric forms in space and mentally perform operations with them.
Enable the student to understand tasks, synthesize ideas, and feel identified with technical language as a means of communication.
Acquire proficiency in handling drawing instruments and sketching parts as a means of quickly and precisely expressing graphic ideas.
That the student knows and values standardization as a universal medium for graphic language.
Ability of spatial vision and knowledge of graphic representation techniques, both by traditional methods of metric geometry and descriptive geometry, and by computer-aided design applications.
Understand and know the fundamental principles governing geometric constructions.
Understand and know the fundamental principles governing representation systems to interpret and represent engineering drawings.
Be able to know and apply representation standards and incorporate the use of technical terms in the language.
Be able to know, understand, and use computer-aided design programs to represent engineering drawings.
Be able to understand, know, and use graphic visualization techniques to improve spatial vision linked to engineering.

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, it is mandatory to obtain a minimum score of 5 out of 10 in the final exam (ETP1) and in the average score of the lab practices (PL) or their exam. Students must attend at least 80% of laboratory practices. The final grade is calculated as 0.5 * ETP1 + 0.1 * PA + 0.2 * PL + 0.2 * TIG. If the minimums are not met, the final grade will be the minimum between the calculated grade and 4.0. Similar rules with adjusted weights and components (ETP2, EPL) apply for extraordinary calls and differentiated assessment.
